prompt: A scheduler’s average throughput is comfortably below capacity, yet millions of jobs become due at midnight. Which planning response is sound?

options.explanation: Wrong. The average hides simultaneous due work and cannot establish a start-time guarantee.

options.text: Measure the due-time burst and provision for its allowed lateness, or obtain permission to spread due times
options.explanation: Correct. Read-ahead prepares work; permitted jitter changes the timing contract.

options.text: Assume reading jobs early makes all external effects instantaneous
options.explanation: Wrong. Dispatch and execution still consume capacity at the allowed start time.

options.text: Silently delay every strict-midnight job by five minutes
options.explanation: Wrong. That changes the tenant’s requested timing without agreement.

workedExample: Inspect the distribution of due occurrences. Read-ahead removes some preparation delay but does not erase a midnight execution burst. Use tenant-approved jitter where possible, and explicitly define lateness, catch-up and retry capacity for the remaining work.

link.title: Executing cron scripts reliably at scale (Slack Engineering)
